<STRUCT_0001>
In this section we discuss some simple criteria which imply that an
algebraic stack is an algebraic space. The main result is that this
happens exactly when objects of fibre categories have no nontrivial
automorphisms. This is not a triviality! Before we come to this
we first do a sanity check.

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme contained in <MATH_0002>.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> A category fibred in groupoids
<MATH_0003>
which is representable by an algebraic space is a Deligne-Mumford stack.
<STRUCT_0003> If <MATH_0004> is an algebraic space over <MATH_0005>, then the associated
category fibred in groupoids
<MATH_0006>
is a Deligne-Mumford stack.
<STRUCT_0004> If <MATH_0007>, then
<MATH_0008> is
a Deligne-Mumford stack.
<STRUCT_0005>

It is clear that (2) implies (3).
Parts (1) and (2) are equivalent by Lemma <REF_0001>.
Hence it suffices to prove (2).
First, we note that <MATH_0001> is stack in sets since
<MATH_0002> is a sheaf (Stacks, Lemma
<REF_0002>).
A fortiori it is a stack in groupoids. Second the diagonal
morphism <MATH_0003>
is the same as the morphism <MATH_0004>
which comes from the diagonal of <MATH_0005>. Hence this is representable
by algebraic spaces according to
Lemma <REF_0003>.
Actually it is even representable (by schemes), as the diagonal of
an algebraic space is representable, but we do not need this.
Let <MATH_0006> be a scheme and let <MATH_0007> be a surjective <ACCENT_0001>tale morphism.
We may think of this as a surjective <ACCENT_0002>tale morphism of algebraic spaces.
Hence by
Lemma
<REF_0004>
the corresponding <MATH_0008>-morphism <MATH_0009>
is surjective and <ACCENT_0003>tale.
